title: Rotated Digits
summary: Determine the count of integers within the range [1, n] that transform into a distinct number when each digit is rotated 180 degrees.
statement: Determine the count of integers within the range [1, n] that transform into a distinct number when each digit is rotated 180 degrees. Valid rotations include 0, 1, and 8 staying the same, 2 and 5 mirroring each other, 6 and 9 mirroring each other, with all other digits becoming invalid.
constraints: Count numbers that remain valid but change after rotating every digit 180 degrees.
hints: A good number uses only rotatable digits and includes at least one digit that changes.
Check each number’s digit set against valid and changed sets.
Accept digits subset of 0125689 and intersection with 2569 nonempty.
The first condition makes rotation defined; the second makes the rotated result different.
editorial: The first condition makes rotation defined; the second makes the rotated result different.

tests.explanation: One remains one, so none qualify.
